record.original_question: Let X be the feature space, let the binary label set be {-1, +1}, let D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m be a dataset sampled from a probability space (D, Sigma, P), and let H be a weak-hypothesis class that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, meaning that H contains the constant classifier h(x) = 1, is closed under negation, and every h in H misclassifies at least one example in D. For Optimal AdaBoost, let w_t in Delta_m denote the example-weight distribution at round t, let err(h; w, D) = sum_{l=1}^m w(l) 1[h(x^(l)) != y^(l)], and let H(w_t, D) = arg min_{h in H} err(h; w_t, D), with the weak learner using a deterministic tie-breaking rule to select a representative hypothesis. Is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P), for any dataset D sampled from P, and for mu-almost all such H, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0, then P-almost surely, for every t > T_0, either H(w_t, D) contains exactly one hypothesis, or every pair of hypotheses in H(w_t, D) agrees on all training examples in D, or the total w_t-weight of the training examples on which two tied optimal hypotheses disagree converges to 0 as t tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: We denote the set of hypotheses that the weak learner that AdaBoost uses, or simply the weak-hypothesis class, by H. We say that H is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D if (1) the hypothesis h, such that, for all x in X, h(x) = 1, is in H; (2) if h in H, then -h in H; and (3) for all h in H, there exists an (x, y) in D such that h(x) != y.

We also assume that the weak learner has a deterministic tie-braking rule; i.e., denoting err(h; w, D) ... and H(w, D) equiv arg min_{h in H} err(h; w, D), for every example weight w that AdaBoost could generate, the weak learner always outputs the same weak hypothesis h* in H(w, D).

Conjecture 1 (No-Ties Conjecture) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, and mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exist m0, T0 > 0, such that if m > m0 is the size of D, then, P-almost surely, either (1), for all t > T0 rounds of Optimal AdaBoost, either (1.a) |H(wt, D)| = 1; or (1.b) for all pairs ht, h't in H(wt, D), ht(x^(l)) = h't(x^(l)) for all l = 1, ..., m; or (2) lim_{t->infty} sum_{l=1}^m wt(l) 1[ht(x^(l)) != h't(x^(l))] = 0, where ht, h't in H(wt, D).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a feature space, and consider binary labels in $\{-1,+1\}$. Let $(\mathcal{D},\Sigma,P)$ be a probability space on labeled examples, and let $D=\{(x^{(l)},y^{(l)})\}_{l=1}^m$ be an i.i.d. sample drawn from $P$. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a class of weak hypotheses $h:\mathcal{X}\to\{-1,+1\}$. Call $\mathcal{H}$ AdaBoost-natural with respect to $D$ if:
(i) the constant hypothesis $h\equiv 1$ belongs to $\mathcal{H}$;
(ii) $h\in\mathcal{H}\Rightarrow -h\in\mathcal{H}$;
(iii) for every $h\in\mathcal{H}$ there exists $(x,y)\in D$ with $h(x)\neq y$.

For a weight vector $w\in\Delta_m$ (the probability simplex on the $m$ training examples) define the weighted training error
$$\mathrm{err}(h;w,D)=\sum_{l=1}^m w(l)\,\mathbf{1}[h(x^{(l)})\neq y^{(l)}],$$
and the set of optimal weak hypotheses
$$\mathcal{H}(w,D)=\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\mathrm{err}(h;w,D).$$
Run Optimal AdaBoost: at each round $t=1,2,\dots$, the weak learner picks (using a fixed deterministic tie-breaking rule) some $h_t\in\mathcal{H}(w_t,D)$, and $w_{t+1}$ is obtained from $w_t$ by the standard AdaBoost reweighting using $h_t$.

Equip the space of probability measures on $(\mathcal{D},\Sigma)$ with a (fixed) measure $\mu$, and likewise equip the space of AdaBoost-natural classes $\mathcal{H}$ with a measure $\mu$ in the natural sense.

Question. Is the following true? For $\mu$-almost every probability space $(\mathcal{D},\Sigma,P)$, for any dataset $D$ sampled from $P$, and for $\mu$-almost every AdaBoost-natural class $\mathcal{H}$, there exist constants $m_0, T_0>0$ such that whenever $m>m_0$, $P$-almost surely either
(1) for every $t>T_0$, one of the following holds:
   (1.a) $|\mathcal{H}(w_t,D)|=1$, or
   (1.b) every pair $h_t,h'_t\in\mathcal{H}(w_t,D)$ satisfies $h_t(x^{(l)})=h'_t(x^{(l)})$ for all $l=1,\dots,m$;
or
(2) for any choice $h_t,h'_t\in\mathcal{H}(w_t,D)$,
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\sum_{l=1}^m w_t(l)\,\mathbf{1}[h_t(x^{(l)})\neq h'_t(x^{(l)})]=0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The No-Ties Conjecture for Optimal AdaBoost is stated as a working conjecture used to establish dynamical-systems and ergodicity properties of Optimal AdaBoost. Subsequent work (e.g., the JMLR paper "Explaining the Success of AdaBoost and Random Forests as Interpolating Classifiers") treats it as a hypothesis under which results are derived rather than as a proven theorem. No published proof refuting or establishing the conjecture in full generality was found.

status_evidence.title: On the Convergence Properties of Optimal AdaBoost
status_evidence.snippet: Provides convergence and ergodicity results for Optimal AdaBoost, conditional on no-ties type assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats no-ties behavior as an assumption rather than a proven fact.

status_evidence.title: Explaining the Success of AdaBoost and Random Forests as Interpolating Classifiers (JMLR)
status_evidence.snippet: Uses the no-ties hypothesis to derive ergodic and convergence results for Optimal AdaBoost.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is used as a hypothesis for further results, not proven.
